name: Somatostatin Analogue (Octreotide LAR or Lanreotide) - GI/pancreatic NET

source.nccn: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Neuroendocrine and Adrenal Tumors
source.textbook: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Somatostatin analogues are used for symptom control (carcinoid/hormonal syndromes) and for antiproliferative tumor control in well-differentiated, SSTR-positive NET. The PROMID trial showed an antiproliferative effect of octreotide LAR in advanced midgut NET. For insulinoma, SSAs should be used only if SSTR-based imaging is positive. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Neuroendocrine and Adrenal Tumors, footnote gg and NE algorithm pages, and DeVita 12th ed.

histology: well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor (low or intermediate grade)
supportiveCare: Somatostatin analogue MONOTHERAPY: give octreotide LAR OR lanreotide (interchangeable, not both), every 4 weeks, continued until progression or intolerance.
For breakthrough carcinoid-syndrome symptoms, add short-acting octreotide 100 to 250 mcg SC three times daily (NCCN line 1355).
Discontinue SSA in non-functional tumors on clinically significant progression; continue for functional tumors for symptom control (NCCN line 1387).
monitoring: symptom/hormonal syndrome control (flushing, diarrhea; chromogranin A / 5-HIAA as indicated)
clinical/radiographic response assessment (SSTR-PET/CT and cross-sectional imaging)
glucose (SSAs can affect glucose homeostasis), gallbladder (cholelithiasis risk with chronic SSA)

doseModificationRules.condition: clinically significant progression in a non-functional tumor
doseModificationRules.text: Discontinue SSA for non-functional tumors on progression; consider above-label dosing, PRRT, everolimus, or other systemic therapy per clinical review (NCCN lines 1387, 606).

drugs.name: Octreotide acetate LAR (depot)
drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) NET v1.2026, footnote gg. Octreotide acetate LAR 20 to 30 mg IM every 4 weeks (day 1 of a 28-day cycle). Modeled dose 30 mg (the NETTER-1 control/maintenance dose per DeVita line 207944). Above-label dosing up to 60 mg once a month is a source-stated option on progression (NCCN line 606). SOMATOSTATIN ANALOGUE MONOTHERAPY: octreotide LAR and lanreotide are interchangeable alternatives - administer ONE agent, not both. For breakthrough symptoms, short-acting octreotide 100 to 250 mcg SC three times daily can be added (NCCN line 1355).

provenance.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Neuroendocrine and Adrenal Tumors
provenance.locator: footnote gg (octreotide acetate LAR 20 to 30 mg IM every 4 weeks); neuroendocrine lines 1353, 1498, 1532, 1592, 1771; above-label up to 60 mg once a month, line 606

drugs.name: Lanreotide (depot / autogel)
drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) NET v1.2026, footnote gg (neuroendocrine lines 1440, 1592, 2118). Lanreotide 120 mg SC every 4 weeks (day 1 of a 28-day cycle). ALTERNATIVE to octreotide LAR (not concurrent) - administer ONE agent. Above-label dosing up to 120 mg every 14 days is a source-stated option in select cases (NCCN line 606).

provenance.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Neuroendocrine and Adrenal Tumors
